transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman, the copilot who tried to take control
of the commercial jet from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week, intended to crash it into Israel's
Ben Gurion Airport, an investigation found.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter, but not authorized to speak publicly
as the investigation is still ongoing, and Pierre's Kat Lonsdorf reports from Tel Aviv.
A source familiar with the investigation told NPR that the copilot who attacked the captain
mid-air intended to fly the plane to Ben Gurion, which was its destination, but then crash
it into the airport.
That source also said it's likely the copilot acted alone.
Officials from both the United Arab Emirates and Israel have said that the incident was
an attempted terrorist attack, although the motive is still unclear.
The copilot is from Oman, according to Israeli officials, raising questions about how he was
allowed to fly a plane heading to Israel.
Israel only allows pilots from countries it has diplomatic relations with to enter its
airspace.
Israel said it's opening an examination into how that happened.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Japanese police have arrested a 20-year-old U.S. Marine suspected of robbing and murdering
a local woman on the island of Okinawa.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports Japan's government has lodged formal complaints with the U.S. government
and military.
Japan's Kyoto news agency quotes police as saying the Marine was seen taking a 39-year-old
woman into a hotel and then leaving alone.
The woman was found dead, apparently strangled to death.
The Marine is suspected of killing her and taking her wallet in backpack, but has denied
all charges.
Japan's foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned U.S. Ambassador George Glass to protest.
Glass said in a social media post that he offered condolences and that the U.S. would
fully cooperate with authorities.
Okinawan media have reported that protests over the incident have taken place in three
cities, organizers are planning demonstrations in Tokyo as well, Anthony Kuhn in PR News
Seoul.
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is throwing its support behind six additional
candidates.
This is ahead of the November midterm elections.
As NPR's Tamara Keith reports, the six candidates are running in districts where Republicans
have an edge.
The committee's red to blue is its top-tier backing for candidates and comes with staff
resources and fundraising support.
All six candidates newly added to the list face challenging races.
Only one is in a district rated by the Cook Political Report as lean Republican.
The others face even longer odds.
For instance, Nevada's second congressional district, where candidate Teresa Benitez-Thompson
earned the red to blue nod.
That district has not elected a Democrat since its creation in the early 1980s.
A spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee said describing that race as competitive
is delusional.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded to German scientists Peter
Hageman and Georg Nagel and American scientist Karl Deseroth.
They're being honored for discoveries leading to better investigations of the brain.
It led to the development of light-controlled switches for nerve cells.
This is helping scientists understand how the brain engages in behavior and its role
in disease.
President Trump is going to campaign in Nebraska today with Republican Senator Pete Ricketts.
The incumbent GOP senator is facing a strong challenge from independent candidate Dan Osborne.
He is supported by Democrats.
Avengers Endgame reclaimed the number one spot on Hollywood's all-time worldwide box office
chart this weekend, and piers Bob Mondello has our details.
Marvel's superhero epic first became the highest-grossing film in history back in 2019, passing Avatar,
which had held that title for ten years.
Then the original Avatar was re-released in 2022 to promote a sequel and earned enough
to reclaim the top spot.
Now, it's Avengers that has a sequel coming, so following the same playbook, Endgame has
been re-released and has retaken the title.
It's a friendly competition, both films are Disney releases, and their jockeying reflects
rising prices more than attendance.
In terms of tickets sold, neither film comes close to Titanic.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
And I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News, from Washington.

Japanese police arrest 20-year-old U.S. Marine suspected of robbing and murdering woman on Okinawa
Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee backs six additional candidates ahead of November midterm elections
Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded to Hageman, Nagel, and Deseroth for brain research discoveries
President Trump to campaign in Nebraska with Republican Senator Pete Ricketts facing independent challenger Dan Osborne
